a_skip_to_main_content_link: A 'skip to main content' link on every page, for keyboard and screen-reader users
ai_answers_are_long_prose_their: AI answers are long prose. Their structure, such as heading levels inside an answer, may not suit screen-reader navigation
an_automated_wcag_2_1_aa: An automated WCAG 2.1 AA check (pa11y) runs on every push against the home page, the legal and info pages and the Tanakh page, in both themes. A failure stops the build.
animations_are_reduced_or_removed_when: Animations are reduced or removed when your operating system's 'reduce motion' setting is on
aria_roles_labels_and_live_region: ARIA roles, labels and live-region announcements on interactive controls, including menus, toggles and the AI answer panel
buttons_and_links_are_at_least: Buttons and links are at least 44×44 px on touch devices
hebrew_pages_are_mirrored_right_to: Hebrew pages are mirrored right to left, not only set in a right-to-left text direction
i_want_shelah_to_work_for: I want Sh'elah to work for people who use a keyboard, a screen reader, zoom or other assistive technology. This page says what is in place, what is not yet, and how to tell me about a problem.
if_something_on_shelah_is_hard: If something on Sh'elah is hard or impossible to use, write to me. Say which page it was, what you were trying to do and, if it matters, which assistive technology you use. I will do my best to reply promptly and fix real barriers.
menus_the_reader_settings_panel_and: Menus, the reader settings panel and dialogs work from the keyboard, with a visible focus indicator
not_every_part_of_shelah_meets: Not every part of Sh'elah meets the standard yet:
see_also_the_terms_of_service: See also the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy.
shelah_is_built_for_current_versions: Sh'elah is built for current versions of Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge, and is meant to work with screen readers such as VoiceOver, NVDA and JAWS. The automated checks run in Chrome only.
shelah_is_built_to_meet_the: Sh'elah is built to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA. That is a target, not a certification. The list of known limitations below shows where it falls short.
some_historical_source_texts_such_as: Some historical source texts, such as scanned or OCR'd Hebrew manuscripts, arrive as-is from the source libraries and can have inconsistent markup
status_is_shown_with_text_or: Status is shown with text or an icon as well as color
text_and_control_contrast_checked_agains: Text and control contrast checked against WCAG AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for controls) in both the light and dark themes
text_size_font_and_line_spacing: Text size, font and line spacing can be changed in the reader settings
these_are_open_items_not_permanent: These are open items, not permanent exceptions. I fix them as I find them.
two_third_party_components_the_sign: Two third-party components, the sign-in widget and the calendar, follow their vendors' own accessibility work, which I do not control
